message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My read is **sinus rhythm at about 65–70 beats/minute, with a right bundle branch block (RBBB) pattern**.

- **Rhythm:** Regular, with a P wave before each heartbeat.
- **Axis and PR interval:** Appear normal.
- **QRS:** Widened, approximately 120–140 milliseconds, with a characteristic pattern in V1 and terminal S waves in the lateral leads—consistent with RBBB.
- **ST–T changes:** T-wave inversion in V1 can occur with RBBB. I don’t see clear acute ST elevation suggesting a STEMI.

RBBB means electrical activation of the right ventricle is delayed. It can be longstanding and incidental; whether it is new and whether you have symptoms matter. [RBBB reference](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8142372/)

These measurements are approximate from the image. A clinician should confirm them and compare with an older ECG. **If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting, seek emergency care even without obvious ST elevation.**

How old are you, why was this ECG taken, and are you having any symptoms?
